ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points D and E are on sides $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, with $DE\parallel BC$. Given that $AE=2$ and $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{1}{3}$, what is the length of $EC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $DE\parallel BC$, \\
hence $\angle ADE=\angle ABC$, $\angle AED=\angle ACB$, \\
therefore $\triangle ADE\sim \triangle ABC$, \\
thus $\frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{AD}{AB}$, \\
given $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{1}{3}$, $AE=2$, \\
thus $AC=6$, \\
hence $EC=AC-AE=6-2=\boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle ABC, A is at the top, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; D is located on side AB, E is located on side AC; segment DE spans the interior of the triangle and is parallel to the base BC. Reasoning: Because DE ∥ BC, the small triangle ADE is similar to the whole triangle ABC. Corresponding sides are proportional, therefore AE/AC = AD/AB. It is known that AD/AB = 1/3, and AE = 2, so 2/AC = 1/3, giving AC = 6. Since E is on AC, EC = AC - AE = 6 - 2 = 4.
